images.filename: Old school house, Rackwick, Hoy, Orkney (exterior 2).jpg
images.caption: The old schoolhouse in Rackwick, Hoy, Orkney in Scotland. Originally opened in 1718(?) the school was replaced in 1879(?) by a newer building next door (now the Rackwick hostel). The old schoolhouse now serves as a small museum with informational signage on the walls, some school furniture, and some farming equipment in the yard. The building is very basic, with bare drystone walls, bare rafters, and large bare stone slabs for the roof!

images.caption: Path to Burnmouth The public toilets here at Rackwick must be strong contenders for the title of most remote in Britain. The path, which continues to Burnmouth and the beach at Rack Wick, is a continuation of the narrow metalled road that leads down to Rackwick but peters out at a small car park.

images.caption: Rackwick Rackwick is the only settlement of any sort on Hoy's west coast. Its history was as a crofting and fishing community but nowadays most of the well scattered cottages are holiday homes. The reality is that few people are prepared to live in such an isolated place, far from most modern services and very bleak in winter. Hoy is geologically different from the rest of Orkney, being mostly composed of resistant upper old red sandstone know as the Hoy sandstone; this gives the island mountainous scenery - although in reality the hills are not especially high.
